notice: Hypothetical inputs checked with the metric calculation code. These are not results from the selected games.

tfs.formula: Plate Appearance Contribution = attributed progress − direct loss − lost opportunity.

cases.title: Strikeout; runner stays on third
cases.explanation: One out before the PA. The batter strikes out and the runner remains on third. The batter loses 1/4; the runner loses 1/2 of remaining opportunity.

cases.title: Third out strands the runner
cases.explanation: Two outs before the PA. The strikeout ends the inning. Charge 1/4 for the batter and 1 for the stranded runner; stranding is not an extra out.

cases.title: Strikeout; runner scores on a passed ball
cases.explanation: One out before the PA. The batter is out; the runner on third scores independently on a passed ball. The hitter gets no progress credit. The actual scored runner has no remaining opportunity to erode.

paq-2.formula: Percentile = 100 × (2 × lower scores + tied scores − 1) / (2 × (population size − 1)).

cases.title: Two PAs tie exactly
cases.explanation: Assume a complete illustrative reference population of four PAs: −1/4, 1/3, 2/6 and 1/2. The middle two tie exactly. Real PAQ uses the eligible selected-season population through the reporting cutoff.

cases.title: Only one eligible PA
cases.explanation: A reference population with one PA cannot define this percentile. An unavailable result is not a zero percentile.
cases.equation: Population size − 1 = 0; the percentile is unavailable.

paq-a.formula: Percentile = 100 × (2 × lower scores + tied scores − 1) / (2 × (population size − 1)).

cases.title: Compare the same base and out state
cases.explanation: The target PA has Plate Appearance Contribution −1/4, with a runner on third and one out immediately before the consequence. Its only illustrative peer in that state has −3/4. A bases-empty PA with no outs is in a different cohort.

offensive-reach.formula: Count distinct trajectories with positive batter-attributed progress.

cases.title: Two trajectories advance
cases.explanation: The batter and one existing runner make positive attributed progress. A third runner has no progress. Count each advancing trajectory once, regardless of how far it advances.

hidden-help-rate.formula: PAs helping another runner with no batter progress / PAs with no batter progress.

cases.title: Help in one of two qualifying PAs
cases.explanation: Across three PAs, two produce no batter progress; one of those helps another runner. The PA with batter progress is outside this denominator.

rally-kill-rate.formula: Runner-on-base PAs directly putting an existing runner out / runner-on-base PAs.

cases.title: One of two opportunities ends a runner’s path
cases.explanation: One of two runner-on-base PAs directly puts an existing runner out. A third PA starts with empty bases and does not enter the denominator.

cases.title: A runner from first is put out
cases.explanation: One of two runner-on-base PAs directly destroys a trajectory beginning at first, costing 1/3. The other costs zero. This isolates destruction from erosion.

opportunity-erosion.formula: Sum of PA lost opportunity / number of PAs.

cases.title: Average two erosion amounts
cases.explanation: Two fully accounted-for PAs have erosion amounts of 1/2 and 1/3. This reports their mean loss of opportunity.

empty-game-rate.formula: Eligible games with no qualifying positive contribution / games with at least one PA.

cases.title: A running-only appearance is outside the denominator
cases.explanation: One game has a PA and no positive contribution; another has a PA and two positive contributions. A third has no PA, so it is ineligible here even though the player can have running statistics.

empty-game-damage.formula: Magnitude of negative Plate Appearance Contribution + independent runner damage during an Empty Game.

cases.title: Batting and running damage in one eligible Empty Game
cases.explanation: Assume the game is completely observed and qualifies as empty. One PA has Plate Appearance Contribution −1/4; an independent running episode contributes −1/3. Damage reports their positive loss magnitude.

contribution-path-diversity.formula: −Σ(channel share × ln(channel share)) / ln(3); each positive play counts once per channel.

cases.title: All three channels used equally
cases.explanation: One hit helps the batter and another runner, so it counts once in each of those channels. A steal adds one runner-to-self play. Diversity describes the mix, not total offensive value.

cases.title: Only one channel used
cases.explanation: All positive plays are in the batter-to-self channel. Concentration in one channel gives diversity zero; it does not mean no contribution occurred.

recovery-quality.formula: Count later nonterminal pitches after the first two-strike state, then take their reference-population percentile.

cases.title: Two extra nonterminal pitches
cases.explanation: Post-pitch strike counts are 0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3. The pitch reaching two strikes and the terminal pitch are excluded from the extra-pitch count. Assume the complete illustrative two-strike population has counts 0, 2 and 4.
cases.equation: 2 extra pitches; the middle of counts 0, 2, 4 has percentile 50.

resolution-depth.formula: Number of intentional acts on the longest supported precedence path.

cases.title: Field, throw, catch, tag
cases.explanation: Assume four distinct intentional acts with supported order: field → throw → catch → tag. Depth counts acts; a single act would have depth one.

defender-breadth.formula: Count distinct defensive agents in the supported resolution structure.

cases.title: Four acts by two defenders
cases.explanation: Defender A fields and throws. Defender B catches and tags. Repeated acts by the same player do not add another defender.

run-construction-depth.formula: Count distinct state-changing episodes along the scoring runner’s admitted continuous trajectory.

cases.title: Single, steal, then score on a double
cases.explanation: Assume complete continuity for the same runner: a single reaches first, a steal reaches second, and a teammate’s double brings the runner home. These are three separate state-changing episodes.

run-construction-breadth.formula: Count distinct offensive players whose supported contributions advance the scoring trajectory.

cases.title: The scorer contributes twice
cases.explanation: The scorer singles and steals, then a teammate doubles the scorer home. The scorer counts once despite two contributions; the teammate adds one.

adjudication-volatility.formula: Overturning dispositions / explicitly resolved mapped reviews.

cases.title: An unresolved review stays outside the denominator
cases.explanation: Of three mapped reviews, one overturns, one resolves without overturning, and one remains unresolved. This describes resolved mapped reviews, not all decisions or umpire accuracy.

review-dependence-rate.formula: Review-dependent operative outcomes / all review-eligible decisions, separately for each mechanism.

cases.title: Traditional replay
cases.explanation: Assume the complete illustrative traditional replay population contains 4 eligible decisions and one operative outcome that depends on review. Merely being reviewed does not establish dependence. The two mechanisms are not pooled.

cases.title: Ball/strike challenges
cases.explanation: Assume the complete illustrative ball/strike challenges population contains 2 eligible decisions and one operative outcome that depends on review. Merely being reviewed does not establish dependence. The two mechanisms are not pooled.

role-realization-breadth.formula: Count the distinct realized kinds among Batter, Baserunner, Pitcher and Fielder.

cases.title: Batting twice and running once
cases.explanation: Assume a complete player-game role population: two acts realize Batter Role and one realizes Baserunner Role. Count realized kinds once; generic parent roles do not add kinds.

paq-2.1.formula: Rank Plate Appearance Contribution first, Two-Strike Extension Rank second, and Resolution Depth third; convert that ordering to a percentile.

cases.title: Process quality breaks a Plate Appearance Contribution tie
cases.explanation: Assume all three PAs are eligible: A has (−3/4, 100, 20), B has (3/2, 0, 1), and C has (3/2, 0, 2). A ranks last despite stronger process scores. C beats B only at the third comparison.
cases.equation: Order A < B < C; B receives percentile 50.
